title: The Folk Humor of the Simpleton (Ka Biria u Biej)
khasi_title: Ka Biria u Biej ha Shnong
cultural_context: A humorous and witty Khasi folk comic song illustrating that excessive pretension and vain posturing lead to embarrassment, celebrating warm village good humor, laughter at weekly markets (Iewduh), and the traditional virtue of modest common sense.
lyrics_khasi:
U biej u la leit sha Iewduh ban thied jain,
U la phong da ka tupia ba jrong kum u phlang;
U kheiñ ialade u riewstad u riewbha,
Pynban u la thut ha ka madan Iewbah!

Ki samla ki la rkhie kynriah kylleng,
Ki tymmen ki la khih la ka khlieh mian-mian;
Ai ngin rkhie, hynrei ngin kynmaw ia ka akor,
Ba ka jingshongkhrein ka jah lada khlem jingstad!
lyrics_english:
The simpleton went down to Iewduh market to buy grand clothes,
He donned a tall comical hat like a stalk of dry reed;
He deemed himself a scholar and a man of great nobility,
Yet he stumbled headlong on the stones of the big market!

The market youth burst out into roaring laughter all around,
The wise elders gently shook their heads with amusement;
Let us laugh in good humor, yet remember proper modesty,
For false pride vanishes quickly where true wisdom is lacking!

stanzas.title: U Biej ha Iewduh (Simpleton at Market)
stanzas.khasi:
U biej u la leit sha Iewduh ban thied jain,
U la phong da ka tupia ba jrong kum u phlang;
U kheiñ ialade u riewstad u riewbha,
Pynban u la thut ha ka madan Iewbah!
stanzas.english: The simpleton went to Iewduh market dressed fine with a comical tall hat, posing as a scholar, yet tripped headlong before all!

stanzas.title: Ka Jinghikai ha la Shnong (The Moral Lesson)
stanzas.khasi:
Ki samla ki la rkhie kynriah kylleng,
Ki tymmen ki la khih la ka khlieh mian-mian;
Ai ngin rkhie, hynrei ngin kynmaw ia ka akor,
Ba ka jingshongkhrein ka jah lada khlem jingstad!
stanzas.english: The youths laughed and elders smiled; let us laugh cheerfully but remember humility, for empty pride fails without true wisdom!

vocabulary.biria: Humorous banter, friendly joking, witty comic satire
vocabulary.iewduh: The historic, legendary grand weekly indigenous market of Shillong
vocabulary.rkhie kynriah: To burst into hearty, uproarious communal laughter
vocabulary.riewstad: A learned scholar, person endowed with wisdom and education
